replies.text:
Automated abuse (brute force / mass signup / flooding / scraping): no sign-in, email, SMS or public form in the design — only "Business users get a reporting dashboard with a free SQL editor"; heavy-query flooding already covered by listed threat 3. Not applicable.
Staff/admin screens rendering other people's content: design mentions no comments, files, tickets or shared profile fields — only reports users build for themselves. Not applicable.
Privileged actions with no record (delete/approve/role change/money): no such actions stated; query attribution gap already covered by listed threat 4.
Cacheable personal/financial pages: nothing in the design about documents, downloads, proxies or CDNs. Not applicable.
Attacker-controlled text into logs, CSV/spreadsheet exports, emails or headers: the design never states an export, email or log sink ("build their own reports" only) — would depend on how it is built. Not applicable.
Single-reviewer items: the missing authentication/authorisation on the editor ("Business users get" with deterministic signal `"auth":false`) is a distinct attack from authorised over-reading — not covered. Export/bulk-download and write/DDL items either depend on unstated build choices or restate listed threats 1 and 2.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-08",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Reporting dashboard", "Free SQL editor", "Production replica"],
    "dataStores": ["production replica"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["internal network -> dashboard", "dashboard -> production replica"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "No authentication or entitlement check stated for reaching the SQL editor",
      "scenario": "The design names only an audience ('business users get' the dashboard) and defines no sign-in, SSO or group check on the editor. Anyone who can reach the internal dashboard URL - a contractor, an intern, an unrelated employee, a compromised laptop or any internal service with network access - loads the free SQL editor and queries the production replica as if they were an entitled reporting user. This is unauthenticated access to production data, distinct from an authorised analyst over-reading tables.",
      "component": "Reporting dashboard / SQL editor entry point",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Business users get a reporting dashboard with a free SQL editor connected to the production replica so they can build their own reports." },
        { "quote": "\"exposure\":\"internal\",\"llmFeatures\":false,\"agentTools\":true,\"paymentFlow\":false,\"secretHandling\":false,\"fileUpload\":false,\"auth\":false" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V4.1.1", "V2.1.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-306", "CWE-862"],
      "plainLanguage": "The design never says users must log in or belong to an approved group, so anyone who finds the dashboard URL inside the network can run queries against production data.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Authenticate and authorise every request to the SQL editor",
        "given": "a request to the reporting dashboard or its SQL execution endpoint",
        "when": "the caller has no authenticated session or is not a member of the approved reporting entitlement group",
        "then": "the request is rejected before any SQL reaches the production replica, and the denial is logged with the caller identity and source"
      }
    }
  ]
}
